help.tips[0].examples[0].en: That's the colleague whose wife is a doctor.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The neighbours whose dog always barks are moving.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The possessor is die Nachbarin (feminine), so 'whose' is deren — followed directly by the noun, no article.
help.tips[0].en.text: der Mann, dessen Auto … · das Kind, dessen Eltern … · die Frau, deren Kinder … · die Leute, deren Haus … Gender/number from the noun before the comma; the noun after dessen/deren has no article.
help.tips[0].en.title: dessen / deren = whose (no ending, no article)
help.tips[0].en.trap: English 'whose' has one form. German has two — dessen (m/n) and deren (f/Pl) — and they are decided by the possessor, not by what is possessed.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: That's the teacher I owe everything to.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Those are the friends I trust most.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: helfen takes the dative, so the masculine relative pronoun is dem.
help.tips[1].en.text: der Mann, dem ich helfe · die Frau, der ich danke · das Kind, dem das Eis schmeckt · die Freunde, denen ich das Buch leihe. If the verb takes the dative, the pronoun does too.
help.tips[1].en.title: dem / der / dem / denen after dative verbs
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: That's the café where we met.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The company I work for has two hundred employees.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Stadt is feminine and 'born in' is a position, so in takes the dative: in der. The preposition comes first.
help.tips[2].en.text: das Haus, in dem ich wohne · die Firma, bei der ich arbeite · die Freunde, mit denen ich reise · der Ort, an dem wir uns getroffen haben · die Stadt, aus der ich komme.
help.tips[2].en.title: Preposition + pronoun: the preposition leads
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: the children I help — the children whose parents work
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: the author whose book I am reading — the singer whose songs I like
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: geben takes the person in the dative; in the plural the relative pronoun is denen, not the article den. deren would mean 'whose'.
help.tips[3].en.text: Beyond the articles, only denen (Dat Pl), dessen and deren are new. Nom der die das die · Akk den die das die · Dat dem der dem denen · Gen dessen deren dessen deren.
help.tips[3].en.title: The full table has three new words
help.vocab[9].en: to get to know each other
help.context.en: I have a friend whose family lives in Vienna and at whose place I stay every year. Her brother, to whom I lent my bike, works in the café where we met. And the neighbours who own the flat above hers are the people whose dog I sometimes walk.
help.hookEn: Say 'the friend whose dog I walk' or 'the café where we met' in one smooth German sentence.
help.introEn: The relative-pronoun table completes here with the genitive: dessen (m/n) and deren (f/Pl) — 'whose'. Der Mann, dessen Auto kaputt ist. Die Frau, deren Kinder hier spielen. Die Leute, deren Haus wir gekauft haben. dessen/deren never change (no ending) and are followed directly by the noun without an article. The dative row — dem, der, dem, denen — comes back with its two triggers: dative verbs (helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, schmecken, leihen with the person) and prepositions that take the dative or the position sense (mit dem, bei denen, in der, aus dem, von dem). And the preposition always leads: das Haus, in dem ich wohne; die Freunde, bei denen ich übernachte. With all four cases in hand, the relative clause is the tool that lets you describe anything at all in one sentence. The quiz gives no case labels: decide from the relative clause itself — a dative verb (helfen, vertrauen, leihen), a preposition, or a noun straight after the gap (then it is dessen / deren).
help.rememberEn[0]: dessen (m/n), deren (f/Pl): whose — then the noun, no article.
help.rememberEn[1]: Dative verb or dative preposition → dem / der / dem / denen.
help.recallEn.known: From "Relativsätze mit Dativ & Präposition": dem, der, denen.
help.recallEn.today: The genitive row: dessen and deren for whose.
sentences[1].whyEn: Possession: deren — the genitive of die ('her car').
sentences[2].whyEn: in + dative for the place: in dem.
sentences[5].whyEn: das Kind → dessen Eltern — dessen for the neuter too.
